messages.content: How far will a car travel in time 't' when launched with velocity 'v' at an angle 'theta'?

function.name: calculate_projectile_range
function.description: Calculate the range of a projectile launched at an angle with initial velocity, using the kinematic equation. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

initial_velocity.description: The initial velocity at which projectile is launched. This is a float type value.

angle.description: The angle at which projectile is launched. This should be in degrees. This is a float type value.

time.description: The time in seconds after which the range is to be calculated. This is a float type value.

message.reasoning: The user asks: "How far will a car travel in time 't' when launched with velocity 'v' at an angle 'theta'?" They want the distance traveled by a car launched with velocity v at angle theta over time t. This is essentially projectile motion. The range formula: R = v^2 * sin(2θ) / g. But they also mention time t. Actually, the distance traveled in time t is horizontal displacement: x = v * cos(theta) * t. But if we consider projectile motion, the vertical component matters for time of flight. But the question: "How far will a car travel in time 't' when launched with velocity 'v' at an angle 'theta'?" That implies horizontal distance traveled in time t: x = v * cos(theta) * t. But maybe they want the range formula? The function provided calculates projectile range given initial velocity, angle, and time. It uses default time 0.5. So we can call the function with initial_velocity=v, angle=theta, time=t.
